Minimum Wage by State 2027: Complete List of New Rates

Direct AnswerMinimum wage by state for 2027: every state new rate, tipped wages, and big-city minimums in one complete table, plus what the changes mean for your pay.

Quick Answer

In 2027, Washington leads the states at $17.73 an hour, while the federal minimum stays $7.25 — find your state’s rate in the full table.

On January 1, 2027, the minimum wage rises in more than a dozen states — while 20 states stay parked at the $7.25 federal floor, unchanged since 2009. Washington leads the states at $17.73 an hour, Washington, D.C. tops everything at $18.40, and Michigan makes one of the year’s biggest jumps to $15.00.

As the technical tools architect at Hourly Wage Converter, I track these rates because they feed the calculators workers use every day. This guide puts every verified 2027 rate in one place: all 50 states plus D.C., tipped wages, the big-city rates that beat their states, and what the new numbers mean for an actual paycheck.

The Short Answer: 2027 in 60 Seconds

  • Highest state: Washington, $17.73/hour (Jan 1, 2027). Connecticut ($17.48) and California ($17.40) are next.
  • Highest anywhere: Washington, D.C., $18.40 (Jan–Jun 2027; the July adjustment is not announced yet).
  • Federal floor: $7.25, unchanged since 2009 — still the legal minimum in 20 states.
  • Biggest jump: Michigan, to $15.00 under a 2025 state law — with more scheduled increases behind it.
  • Biggest surprise: New York gets no 2027 increase; its inflation off-ramp froze rates at $17.00 downstate / $16.00 upstate.
  • Tipped workers: the federal tipped cash wage stays $2.13, but eight states allow no tip credit at all — tipped workers there earn the full minimum.

The Biggest 2027 Changes (and Surprises)

Most 2027 increases are inflation adjustments of 3–4%. The interesting moves are the exceptions:

  • Michigan → $15.00. A 2025 state law (PA 9) reset the schedule: $15.00 on Jan 1, 2027, with the tipped wage at $6.30 (42% of the full rate). One of the year’s largest dollar jumps.
  • Nebraska → $15.26. Lawmakers replaced the voter-approved CPI formula with a fixed 1.75% annual increase starting 2027 — a slower climb than voters chose. Local ordinances trying to restore CPI-based increases are in litigation.
  • Virginia → $13.75. A 2026 law fixed $13.75 for 2027 and $15.00 for 2028, with inflation indexing resuming in 2029.
  • New York: no increase. The state’s inflation off-ramp triggered, freezing rates at $17.00 downstate and $16.00 elsewhere — a proposed further hike was not approved.
  • Missouri: frozen at $15.00. A 2025 law repealed the inflation indexing voters approved, so the rate holds flat.
  • Oklahoma: voters said no. A June 2026 ballot measure to reach $15 was defeated, so the state stays at $7.25.
  • Alaska’s timing quirk: its $15.00 rate takes effect July 1, 2027 — not January 1 — under the ballot-measure schedule. Hawaii, meanwhile, holds at $16.00 through 2027 with $18.00 coming January 1, 2028.

Tipped Minimum Wages for 2027

The federal tipped cash wage stays at $2.13 — but that number matters less than most people think. Eight states (Alaska, California, Minnesota, Montana, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, plus Hawaii’s limited credit) allow no tip credit at all, so tipped workers there earn the full minimum wage before tips. D.C. continues phasing its tip credit out: the 2027 tipped wage is $10.30, not yet the full $18.40.

Notable 2027 tipped cash wages: Arizona $12.65, Colorado $12.69, Florida $11.98, Illinois $9.00, Maine $7.85, Michigan $6.30, New Jersey $6.61, Ohio $5.70, South Dakota $6.15. If you earn tips, also read our no-tax-on-tips guide — the 2025–2028 federal deduction is a separate benefit from the wage floor itself.

Frequently Asked Questions About 2027 Minimum Wage

Answers to the six questions readers ask most are collected here; each also appears in the page’s structured data.

What is the federal minimum wage in 2027?

The federal minimum wage stays at $7.25 an hour in 2027 — unchanged since 2009. It applies in the 20 states with no higher state rate, and the federal tipped cash wage stays at $2.13. Where a state or city sets a higher rate, the higher rate is the one your employer must pay.

Which state has the highest minimum wage in 2027?

Washington, at $17.73 an hour effective January 1, 2027. Connecticut ($17.48) and California ($17.40) follow. Washington, D.C. is higher than any state at $18.40 (January through June 2027), and several Washington cities — Burien ($22.49), Tukwila ($22.45), Renton ($22.28), Seattle ($22.14) — top every statewide rate.

Did New York raise its minimum wage for 2027?

No. New York’s inflation “off-ramp” triggered, so the 2027 rates hold at the 2026 levels: $17.00 in New York City, Long Island, and Westchester, and $16.00 in the rest of the state. A proposal to raise it further was not approved.

What is Michigan’s minimum wage in 2027?

Michigan jumps to $15.00 an hour on January 1, 2027 under PA 9 of 2025 — one of the year’s biggest increases. The tipped minimum moves to $6.30 (42% of the full rate). Missouri, by contrast, stays flat at $15.00 after its legislature repealed inflation indexing.

Do cities have their own minimum wage in 2027?

Yes — dozens of cities and counties set rates above their state’s. The highest confirmed for 2027 include Burien, Washington ($22.49), Tukwila ($22.45), Renton ($22.28), Seattle ($22.14), and West Hollywood, California ($20.94). Always check the city rate where you actually work; it overrides the state rate.

How much does full-time minimum wage pay per year in 2027?

At 40 hours a week for 52 weeks: Washington’s $17.73 pays $36,878 a year; a $15.00 rate pays $31,200; the $7.25 federal floor pays $15,080 — all before taxes and deductions. Use our paycheck calculator to see what a 2027 rate means per pay period.

Key Takeaways & Action Plan

  • Know your real floor: check the city rate where you work, not just the state — Burien’s $22.49 beats Washington’s $17.73 by nearly $5.
  • Watch the calendar: most 2027 rates start January 1, but Alaska’s $15.00 starts July 1 — and D.C. adjusts again mid-year.
  • Tipped workers: eight states pay you the full minimum before tips; everywhere else, confirm the cash wage — $2.13 federal is the floor, not the norm.
  • Turn the rate into a paycheck: run your state’s 2027 rate through the paycheck calculator to see gross pay per period.
  • Bookmark this page: Oregon, Vermont, and several big cities had not announced 2027 rates as of October 2026 — this table will be updated as they land.

Calculation Methodology & Sources

State rates were verified in October 2026 against state labor department announcements, official 2027 wage schedules, and the Federal Register (federal contractor rates). Annual-pay figures use 40 hours × 52 weeks ($17.73 × 2,080 = $36,878; $15.00 × 2,080 = $31,200; $7.25 × 2,080 = $15,080), gross pay before taxes and deductions. Oregon and Vermont 2027 rates were unannounced at verification time; several city 2027 rates likewise. This article is general education, not legal or tax advice. To model the paycheck a 2027 rate produces, use our Paycheck Calculator or browse the Calculator Directory.

3 Things to Remember

  1. Highest state: Washington, $17.73 an hour (January 1, 2027); Connecticut ($17.48) and California ($17.40) follow.
  2. Highest anywhere: Washington, D.C., at $18.40 (January through June 2027).
  3. Federal floor: $7.25, unchanged since 2009 — still the legal minimum in 20 states; the federal tipped cash wage stays $2.13.

Methodology & Data Verification

  • Basis: Pay figures are gross unless a section states take-home; tax figures use 2026 federal rules where shown.
  • Method: Full formulas, baselines, and rounding rules are on our calculation methodology page.
  • Coverage: U.S. federal rules; state and local rules vary and are not included.
  • Review: Last updated October 23, 2026.
  • Disclaimer: Estimates for planning only — not tax or legal advice.
